I have generated and saved a method comparison synthesis on the modular pipeline, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning approaches in our papers. The synthesis titled "Comparison of Modular Pipeline and Imitation Learning Performance in Autonomous Driving" (ID: af66ce35-cb72-53fb-b45e-d33f7e7da2b8) highlights the following:

- Modular pipeline and imitation learning performances differ by less than 10%.
- Modular pipeline performance is bimodal, dependent on perception stack success, and underperforms in new town and weather conditions due to perception failures.
- Imitation learning benefits from imitation dropout techniques and mid-level representations, but pure imitation learning alone is insufficient even with large datasets.
- Mid-level representations enable cross-domain training and closed-loop simulation testing.

This comparison synthesis integrates complementary insights on strengths, limitations, and training strategies of these approaches. If you want, I can also generate a comparison including reinforcement learning more explicitly or a full review draft.
